behaviours.name: rollup.cut_excludes_releases
behaviours.what: a task's reported `cut` is the cut it is in, never a release that closes it

behaviours.name: traces.table_rows
behaviours.what: a `traces` anchor may name a table row by its first cell

behaviours.name: verdict.summary_agrees_with_exit_code
behaviours.what: the `ok`/`failed` word and the reported counts are what blocked, not every finding

behaviours.name: ready.order_is_derived
behaviours.what: `ready` answers in a derived rank (what a task releases, then the critical path, then the chain of work behind it, then effort) rather than in id order, and `--explain` says which

behaviours.name: paths.unmatched_needs_evidence
behaviours.what: `APLAN019` reports a dead `paths` glob only where the task cites a `commit`, `file` or `test`, so a plan that names trees a later cut creates is silent

behaviours.name: paths.unmatched_ignores_a_bound_sibling
behaviours.what: `APLAN019` is silent about a dead `paths` glob when the task's cited commit or file binds through another one, so a stale declaration does not refuse a close

behaviours.name: ready.reports_a_closeable_cut
behaviours.what: `ready` names a cut whose members are all done rather than answering with silence

behaviours.name: mutation.refused_when_check_would_reject
behaviours.what: a command or tool that writes runs the rules against the plan it would produce, and refuses a mutation that introduces a finding

behaviours.name: verify.one_tasks_defect_does_not_stop_the_run
behaviours.what: a defect in one task's input, or in one configured command, is a finding rather than a reason to abandon the run and report nothing about the rest

behaviours.name: verify.configured_commands_are_bounded
behaviours.what: a configured `test.list` or `url.check` that does not return is killed at its limit and reported, rather than waited for

behaviours.name: ready.honours_a_declared_preference
behaviours.what: `ready` offers a task after the offered tasks its `prefer_after` names, without ever blocking it

behaviours.name: milestone.members_are_live_work
behaviours.what: `APLAN021` counts a cut's members as live work, so a cut left holding only other cuts, or only cancelled tasks, is reported rather than silent

behaviours.name: cut.named_by_id_or_label
behaviours.what: a `--cut` argument may be the milestone id or the label the cut reports itself under, on every command that takes one

behaviours.name: supersede.successor_is_placed_and_classified
behaviours.what: a successor inherits the predecessor's subject tags and is judged in the cut `--cut` names, so `supersede` itself can repair a plan that requires a tag family and a cut membership

behaviours.name: import.carries_the_plans_vocabulary
behaviours.what: `import` gives every task it writes the tags the invocation names, and says which declared `tag_families` member the import would otherwise leave missing, so a plan with a mandatory vocabulary can be imported into

behaviours.name: milestone.release_holds_cuts
behaviours.what: a milestone tagged `release` holds the cuts it closes: `APLAN021` accepts it and `roadmap` rolls up their work rather than reporting none

behaviours.name: rollup.carries_effort
behaviours.what: `roadmap` and `summary` report the effort behind their counts, and divide it into weeks where `effort_days_per_week` is declared

behaviours.name: config.explicitly_selectable
behaviours.what: `--config <file>` reads exactly that file and discovers none, `--no-config` reads none at all, and a named file that is missing is an error rather than a fallback

behaviours.name: close.evidence_resolves_before_write
behaviours.what: `close` resolves a proposed citation before it writes, on both surfaces; only `--no-resolve` opts out, and it says what it skipped

behaviours.name: paths.no_sample_is_not_a_zero
behaviours.what: `aplan paths` reports that nothing was sampled rather than a share of 0%, and a task whose `paths` do not compile is left unmeasured rather than counted as zero

behaviours.name: verify.reports_what_nothing_checked
behaviours.what: `verify` reports the citations its configuration gave it no resolver for, rather than counting them as resolved

behaviours.name: add.reads_a_task_list
behaviours.what: `aplan add --from <file>` adds every task a file names as one change, each entry resolved against the ones before it

behaviours.name: evidence.file_path_is_normalised
behaviours.what: a path is read the same way wherever a plan writes one: a `file` citation, a `paths` glob and a `traces` target all resolve however it is spelled (`./x`, `a/../x`)

behaviours.name: evidence.file_names_a_section
behaviours.what: a `file` citation may name the section that proves it (`file:docs/report.md#result`), resolved against that document's own headings and table rows at the cited rev, so a written decision is citable as evidence rather than only as a file that exists

behaviours.name: facts.reports_which_build
behaviours.what: `aplan facts --identity` names this build -- its version, the commit it was built from, and the digests of its capability document and its own image -- without needing a plan, a repository or a clean tree

behaviours.name: output.plan_text_cannot_steer_a_terminal
behaviours.what: a control character in any field a plan supplies is replaced by a visible marker before it reaches a human rendering, at every `--color` setting, while the machine formats keep the bytes the plan holds

behaviours.name: contract.begin_marker_matched_by_prefix
behaviours.what: the generated block's opening marker is recognised by its start: a line opening `<!-- aplan:begin`, then a space or a dash, and closing `-->`, which writing the block replaces with the full marker

behaviours.name: color.explicitly_selectable
behaviours.what: `--color=auto|always|never` overrides the terminal detection in both directions, reaching everything the tool prints -- its findings, its refusals, and `clap`'s own usage errors -- while the machine formats stay byte-identical at every setting

behaviours.name: traces.structured_documents
behaviours.what: a `traces` anchor may address a node of a YAML or JSON document, as a JSON Pointer (`#/states/provisioning`) or a JSONPath (`#$.states.provisioning`)

behaviours.name: traces.unstamped_is_reported
behaviours.what: a `done` task that stamps none of its anchored `traces` is reported by `APLAN028`, rather than exempt as a task closed before drift was enabled

behaviours.name: generated.names_the_build_that_wrote_it
behaviours.what: a generated `ROADMAP.status.md` and `AGENTS.md` block carry a comment naming the version and surface that wrote them, and a drift report names the build doing the checking

behaviours.name: why.cut_bounded_by_default
behaviours.what: `aplan why` reports an unfinished cut as itself rather than walking into its members, and names the traversal that produced every answer; `--all` asks for the complete closure

behaviours.name: identity.reads_a_per_user_file
behaviours.what: a claimant's name may come from a per-user file outside the repository, read between the environment variable and git's `user.name`, and holding nothing a rule reads

behaviours.name: ids.sequential_survives_concurrent_writers
behaviours.what: a command that mints an id re-reads the plan and mints again when another writer takes it first, so concurrent writers do not serialise on the id

commands.about: Validate the plan. Fails on any error. Reads `.aplan.yml` if present; flags below override it
commands.name: check

commands.about: Resolve evidence against the git repository (L1/L2, and L3 with `--execute`). Unlike `check`, this opens the repo: a `commit` must exist and touch the task's `paths`, a `file` must exist at the cited rev, a `test` must be one the configured runner lists
commands.name: verify

commands.about: List tasks whose blockers are all `done`, best first
commands.name: ready

commands.about: Parked tasks whose `revisit_at` has arrived: a hand-off to a scheduler
commands.name: due

commands.about: Explain what is blocking a task: its own blockers, and any unfinished cut
commands.name: why

commands.about: What the plan says the next version must be
commands.name: version

commands.about: Print the dependency graph as Mermaid, whole or scoped
commands.name: graph

commands.about: Show one task whole: its fields, what it waits on and releases, and the findings currently attached to it
commands.name: show

commands.about: Show one task's neighbourhood: what must precede it, and what it releases
commands.name: tree

commands.about: Measure how much of recent history each task's `paths` would match
commands.name: paths

commands.about: Report what each rule could actually have failed on
commands.name: vacuity

commands.about: Report live tasks that have sat unchanged, and which of them could start
commands.name: stale

commands.about: Report the deprecation runways this plan declares
commands.name: deprecations

commands.about: Record what this plan proved, bound to the commit it proved it at
commands.name: attest

commands.about: Write the agent contract this repository's policy implies
commands.name: export-agents-md

commands.about: Write the plan's statuses back into a `roadmap.json` contract
commands.name: export-roadmap-json

commands.about: Write the plan out in somebody else's shape
commands.name: export

commands.about: Check that a document names tasks that exist
commands.name: check-docs

commands.about: Roll the plan up by phase: tasks, effort, and how many are ready
commands.name: summary

commands.about: Drop a task, or a whole cut, recording the decision rather than deleting the record of it. Refuses to revive anything already terminal
commands.name: drop

commands.about: Record who is working on a task, so two actors sharing a repository can see it. Refuses to take a task somebody else holds unless `--from` names them, and refuses to overwrite a claim made between reading and writing
commands.name: claim

commands.about: Drop a claim, naming whose it was. Anybody may run it, so a claim nobody released can always be cleared; the record of who held it is in the diff
commands.name: release

commands.about: Record that work on a task has started. The claim is checked against the repository afterwards, so this is a statement `verify` can contradict rather than one it takes on trust
commands.name: start

commands.about: Record that work on a task has stopped, returning it to `todo`. Not a closure: nothing is claimed about the work, which is what `close` is for
commands.name: stop

commands.about: Move tasks between cuts, editing both milestones or neither
commands.name: mv

commands.about: Emit the plan's tasks as data, so a rollup this tool does not have is a `jq` line rather than a feature request. Carries what a rollup needs resolved: the cut a task belongs to, and whether it is ready
commands.name: tasks

commands.about: Show the critical path: the longest `effort_days`-weighted chain of dependent tasks. Advisory, never a gate
commands.name: critical-path

commands.about: Render the plan grouped by cut (the milestones): per-cut rollups, the critical path, and cross-cutting tasks. Advisory: it reports, and never fails a build
commands.name: roadmap

commands.about: Close a task: set it `done` and attach evidence, in place. With no `--evidence`, records the current `HEAD` commit
commands.name: close

commands.about: Repair a closed task's evidence: add, replace or remove a citation, in place, without reopening it
commands.name: amend

commands.about: File the successor to a closed task whose traced outcome no longer holds, and re-stamp the closed one as reviewed
commands.name: supersede

commands.about: Add or remove a dependency edge: `dep add A --after B` means A comes after B, and `dep rm` takes it back
commands.name: dep

commands.about: Add, remove or rename a tag: `tag add A cli`, `tag rm A cli`, and `tag rename epic-a epic-b` across every task that carries it
commands.name: tag

commands.about: Import proposals from another tool's format into `aplan` tasks. Lossy by design, and says so: every field the task model cannot hold is reported
commands.name: import

commands.about: Scaffold a new task file: the next id in this plan's own convention, the fields `check` needs, and a body to fill in. It fills in nothing it cannot know, so a new task carries no estimate and no evidence unless you give them. `--from <file>` adds every task a file names instead, as one change
commands.name: add

commands.about: Run an MCP server over stdio, exposing a deliberately small tool set (`identity`, `ready`, `why`, `check`, `verify`, `add`, `show`, `dep`, `close`, `claim`, `release`, `start`, `stop`) to an agent. `close` goes through the same evidence gate as the CLI, in both directions: an agent cannot close through MCP what it could not close here, and is not refused what this command records
commands.name: mcp

commands.about: Scaffold a starter `.aplan.yml`, refusing to overwrite an existing one
commands.name: init

commands.about: Print this tool's facts as JSON: its rules, output formats, commands, and evidence kinds, generated from the code (the source for `facts.json`)
commands.name: facts

commands.about: Print the JSON Schema derived from the Rust types
commands.name: schema

mcp_tools.description: Name the build of this server: its version, the commit it was built from, and the digests of its capability document and its own image. Asking an installed CLI does not answer this -- a configured MCP process may be a different executable, which is how a pilot spent a pass on a defect the checkout had already fixed. Needs no plan and no repository.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_identity

mcp_tools.description: List tasks whose blockers are all done, so an agent can pick real work.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_ready

mcp_tools.description: Explain what is blocking a task: its own blockers, and any unfinished cut, without expanding that cut's membership. Pass `all` for the complete transitive closure; every answer names its `traversal`.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_why

mcp_tools.description: Validate the plan and return its diagnostics, and `denied`: whether this plan fails the build under the repository's warning policy. Hermetic: no git, no network.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_check

mcp_tools.description: Resolve the plan's evidence against the repository (L1/L2): a cited commit must exist and touch the task's `paths`, a cited file must exist. Opens git. Never runs tests.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_verify

mcp_tools.description: Create a task: the next id in this plan's own convention (or its prefix and a ULID, where the repository set `id_strategy: ulid`), placed in a cut, whose `phase` it takes. Refuses before writing what `check` would reject after, by running the rules on the plan this would produce; what it would only warn about is named in `notes` instead.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_add

mcp_tools.description: One task whole: its `paths`, `traces` and `evidence`, which no other tool returns, plus what the graph resolves (its cut, whether it is ready, what it waits on and what it releases) and every finding attached to it. Reads the evidence ladder, so a closed task whose citation rotted looks different from a healthy one.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_show

mcp_tools.description: Add or remove one dependency edge: `after` is the task that must finish first. `blocked_by` is the only ordering the model has and it was writable only at creation, so re-sequencing meant editing files by hand. Refuses before writing what `check` would reject after: a cycle, an id that does not exist, a cancelled blocker, or a done task acquiring an unfinished one. A milestone's `blocked_by` is which tasks are in that cut rather than what it comes after, so editing that is refused here and belongs to `aplan mv`.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_dep

mcp_tools.description: Close a task with evidence, resolved before it is written: a cited commit must exist and touch the task's `paths`, a cited file must exist, and a cited test must be one a configured runner lists. Refuses exactly what the CLI refuses; evidence is a citation to be resolved, never a score the caller asserts. It never runs a test and never fetches a url, and whatever nothing here could check is named in `unchecked` rather than left looking like a pass. `aplan_verify` resolves the whole plan.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_close

mcp_tools.description: Record that you are working on a task, so other agents sharing this repository can see it and `aplan_ready` can be filtered to what nobody holds. Two agents cannot both be told they hold one task: the write is a compare-and-swap, and the second is refused rather than overwriting the first. Taking a task somebody holds needs `from` naming them, which is checked. The name comes from `as`, else `APLAN_OWNER`, else the repository's git user, else the operating system's; it is never read from `.aplan.yml`, because several actors share one repository.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_claim

mcp_tools.description: Drop a claim, reporting whose it was. Any caller may release, because a claim lasts until it is released or taken over and an abandoned one has to be clearable by somebody else; the record of who held it is in the diff. Releasing a task nobody holds changes nothing and says so.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_release

mcp_tools.description: Record that work on a task has begun, setting `in_progress`. A claim rather than a proof, and checked like one: `aplan_verify` reports `APLAN053` where the repository holds nothing matching the task's `paths`, so a status nobody acted on does not pass as progress. Refuses a task that is already terminal, because nothing reopens finished work.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_start

mcp_tools.description: Record that work on a task has stopped, returning it to `todo`. Not a closure: it claims nothing about what was done, which is what `aplan_close` is for. Refuses a task that is not `in_progress`, since there is then nothing to stop.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_stop

rules.title: frontmatter parses and satisfies the schema
task ids are unique
blocked_by references a task that exists
the dependency graph is acyclic
done carries at least one piece of evidence
no task blocks itself
a done task does not depend on an unfinished one
traces anchors resolve to a real heading or node
active tasks carry an effort estimate
a note used as evidence carries a date
commit evidence resolves to a commit in this repository
commit evidence touches at least one of the task's paths
test evidence names a test the runner can find
test evidence names a test that passes
file evidence resolves at the cited rev
url evidence answers when it is checked
done evidence meets the configured minimum strength
a closed task's traced section is unchanged since closure
a task's paths globs each match at least one tracked file, once it cites evidence
a live task is not blocked by a dropped one
a milestone has members and carries no effort or paths
every task is a member of exactly one cut, or is tagged cross-cutting
a done task's path-checkable evidence can actually be path-checked
a done task's commit evidence is about that task, not mostly about other work
a cited test belongs to the part of the repository this task's `paths` cover
a tag that looks like a member of a declared family is one
a cancelled cut's members are cancelled too
a done task stamps every trace that can be stamped
a declared tag family is carried by at least one task
a task carries the number of members a declared family requires
file evidence names a file inside the task's paths
a task's paths entries are globs this tool can compile
a prefer_after entry names a task that can actually be preferred
a traces target outside this repository is declared as external
commit evidence names a commit that did work, not a merge
a configured test runner lists at least one test, or says it expects none
a test that passed under `--execute` is distinguishable from one the runner never ran
a `done` task has answered the acceptance criteria its own body states
a `done` task has not ticked a prompt this tool wrote as though it were a criterion
a task declares each `paths` entry once
the generated `AGENTS.md` block says what this repository's policy says
a `revisit_at` names a real instant, on a task that is parked
a live task carries the scaffold's own prompt beside the criteria its author wrote
a closed task claims less of the released version than its level implies, without saying why
a live task's traced section is unchanged since the task was last touched
a done task's ratifiers are done
a `contains` names a milestone that exists, and closes no loop
the released version has moved as far as the closed tasks require
the artifact agrees with what the plan claims about compatibility
a recorded `version` is on a release, and is a version this tool can read
a tag is not one edit from a word that changes what this tool does
`cross-cutting` is not on a task that is a member of a cut
a task that is `in_progress` has something in the repository to show for it
